newsitem.title: USA: PECO Energy CEO-Maine Yankee purchase not probable.
newsitem.headline: PECO Energy CEO-Maine Yankee purchase not probable.

text.p: PECO Energy Co is not likely to buy the struggling Maine Yankee nuclear power plant, PECO president and CEO Corbin McNeill said Thursday.
"We're continuing to have discussions with Maine Yankee," McNeill said at the Nuclear Energy Institute's annual meeting.
"It is not a highly probable one, but we're giving it some review," he said, referring to comments by Maine Yankee chairman David Flanagan that a transaction would be difficult.
McNeill declined to say when PECO Energy would make a decision about the plant.

Flanagan announced earlier this week that Maine Yankee was considering permanently closing its 910 megawatt nuclear power plant in Wiscasset, Maine, and would slash spending on the unit until its future was decided.
The 25-year-old plant has been shut since last December for extensive repairs and upgrades which must be carried out before the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) will allow it to return to service.
Officials estimated that restarting the plant would cost $191 million, and Flanagan said the unit could not be restarted as first projected by early August.

Maine Yankee is 38-percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
